title: Study Skills
subject: Learning skills
description: Make room for your next big idea. Build better habits for taking notes, finding focus, and making what you learn stick.

title: World History
subject: History
description: Follow the connections between people, places, and ideas, from early farming communities to our global world.

title: Biology
subject: Science
description: Explore the living world, from tiny cells to whole ecosystems. Discover how life works, changes, and connects us all.

title: Astronomy
subject: Science
description: Look up, then look closer. Explore planets, stars, galaxies, and the questions that help us understand our place in the universe.

title: Philosophy
subject: Humanities
description: Make room for big questions about knowledge, reality, and how to live. Practice following an argument and looking at an idea from another angle.

title: Computer Science
subject: Technology
description: Find out what happens beneath the screen. Follow the ideas behind computers, from logic gates and programs to networks and the web.

title: Chemistry
subject: Science
description: Explore atoms, bonds, and reactions to understand what matter is made of and how it changes.

title: Psychology
subject: Social sciences
description: Explore how we think, learn, and relate to one another, from the workings of the brain to the influence of a group.

title: Economics
subject: Social sciences
description: Follow the choices behind markets, money, and public policy. Connect everyday decisions with the forces shaping an economy.

title: U.S. History
subject: History
description: Trace the people, conflicts, and ideas that shaped the United States, from early encounters through the Obama presidency.

title: Physics
subject: Science
description: Explore motion, energy, waves, and electricity. Connect everyday observations with the laws that describe our physical world.

title: Linguistics
subject: Humanities
description: Discover how languages work, from sounds and sentence structure to meaning, social connections, and the ways language changes.

title: Statistics
subject: Mathematics
description: Make sense of data, chance, and uncertainty. Learn how to ask better questions about numbers, studies, and predictions.

title: Media Literacy
subject: Social sciences
description: Look closely at the messages around you. Explore who makes media, how it influences us, and how to participate thoughtfully.

title: Ecology
subject: Science
description: Follow the connections between organisms and their environments, from growing populations to ecosystems and conservation.

title: Art History
subject: Humanities
description: Learn to look closely at art and ask how it connects people, places, and ideas. Explore the stories behind objects, images, and the ways we value them.

title: Anatomy & Physiology
subject: Science
description: Explore the structures and systems that keep a human body working, from cells and tissues to movement, breathing, and immunity.

title: Engineering
subject: Technology
description: Explore how people turn scientific ideas into useful things. Follow the design choices behind materials, machines, infrastructure, and new technologies.

title: Artificial Intelligence
subject: Technology
description: Explore how machines learn, recognize patterns, and make decisions. Follow the ideas behind neural networks, robotics, and algorithmic fairness, with numbered coding labs along the way.

title: Navigating Digital Information
subject: Learning skills
description: Build better habits for checking what you read online. Practice evaluating sources, looking for evidence, and finding context before sharing a claim.

title: Intellectual Property
subject: Social sciences
description: Explore copyright, patents, and trademarks, and the questions they raise about creativity, ownership, and sharing ideas.

title: Public Health
subject: Science
description: Explore how communities protect and improve health. Connect biology, environments, social conditions, and policy with the health of whole populations.

title: Film History
subject: Humanities
description: Follow the story of cinema, from early cameras and silent films to Hollywood, world cinema, and documentary. Discover how movies developed their own language.

title: Business: Entrepreneurship
subject: Social sciences
description: Explore how a business idea becomes something people can use. Learn about customers, testing products, building relationships, and deciding how to grow.

title: Geography
subject: Social sciences
description: Explore how Earth works and how people shape it, from weather and oceans to migration, borders, and cities.

title: Sociology
subject: Social sciences
description: Look at the patterns behind everyday life: culture, social groups, inequality, institutions, and the societies we build together.

title: U.S. Government & Politics
subject: Social sciences
description: Understand the U.S. political system, from the Constitution and branches of government to elections, civil rights, and public policy.

title: Organic Chemistry
subject: Science
description: Build on chemistry with carbon compounds, molecular structures, reaction mechanisms, and the chemistry behind materials and medicines.

title: Film Criticism
subject: Humanities
description: Look closely at fifteen films to explore how editing, sound, performance, and visual choices shape the stories we see on screen.

title: European History
subject: History
description: Trace Europe’s changing societies, ideas, revolutions, and conflicts, from the medieval world to the modern era.

title: World Mythology
subject: Humanities
description: Meet creation stories, heroes, tricksters, and monsters from around the world, and explore what myths reveal about the people who tell them.

title: Theater & Drama
subject: Humanities
description: Explore the history and craft of live performance, from ancient stages and dramatic traditions to Shakespeare and Broadway musicals.

title: Business: Soft Skills
subject: Social sciences
description: Practice the people side of work: communication, collaboration, negotiation, job interviews, time management, and avoiding burnout.

title: History of Science
subject: History
description: Follow how people across cultures have investigated the world, from ancient astronomy and medicine to genetics, computing, and climate science.
